BL420 — Session-tracker git repo growth OOM-kills the whole datawatch daemon.

INCIDENT (confirmed live, 2026-10-13): the datawatch daemon OOM-killed itself twice in ~90 minutes. systemd: "The kernel OOM killer killed some processes in this unit" / "Failed with result 'oom-kill'" / "107.4G memory peak" then "106.9G memory peak". It was a crash loop: each restart re-triggered the same commit on the same bloated repo, OOM-killing again.

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed via direct process/cgroup inspection, not assumed):
- internal/session/tracker.go's commit path (commit() around line 598-609) runs `git add -A` then `git commit -m <msg> --allow-empty` on EVERY tracked session event (every input sent, every output recorded, etc.), via the Tracker type documented at the top of the file ("Tracker manages the per-session git-tracked folder").
- There is no .gitignore / exclusion for output.log, which OutputLogPath() (line ~441-444) documents as "Full claude-code output (live)" — an ever-growing, append-only file for a long-lived session.
- There is no repo-size or gc management at repo init (git init / config user.email / user.name, lines ~32-42) — no gc.auto tuning, no pack memory limits.
- Over the life of a long-running session, `git add -A` + commit snapshots the full, growing output.log repeatedly. Until a gc/repack happens, these are stored as separate large loose objects. Eventually git's own default gc.auto threshold (loose object count) trips implicitly on a subsequent `git add -A && git commit`, spawning `git gc --auto` -> `git repack -d -l --no-write-bitmap-index` -> `git pack-objects --local --delta-base-offset --honor-pack-keep ... --keep-true-parents --non-empty --all --reflog --indexed-objects --unpacked --incremental`.
- pack-objects' delta search across many large near-duplicate blobs is memory-hungry and uncapped by default (no pack.windowMemory limit set anywhere). Confirmed directly: this process hit 108GB+ RSS before being killed, on a host with 122GB RAM + 8GB swap (swap was fully exhausted at the time).
- Confirmed via `/proc/<pid>/cgroup` that this git subprocess runs INSIDE the datawatch.service cgroup (it's a descendant of the daemon process, spawned by the tracker), so when it exhausts memory, the kernel OOM killer takes down the whole cgroup — the entire daemon, every session, everything — not just the git subprocess.
- Scale of the problem confirmed directly: of 322 total session repos under ~/.datawatch/sessions/*/, most are tiny (one session = one commit = ~212K), but long-lived sessions are not: local-node-ab22 is 30GB/.git (3488 commits, 2285 reflog entries) — a long-lived session that was never cleaned up; local-node-9245 is 8.7GB (2107 commits) and still actively growing right now; local-node-ddeb is 815MB (652 commits). Any of these can trip the same trap again.

IMMEDIATE STOPGAP ALREADY APPLIED DIRECTLY, OUTSIDE THIS PRD (do not redo, but verify it's still in place and durable — currently it's only live git config, not yet code):
1. Killed the runaway pack-objects/repack process tree that was mid-flight.
2. Set `git config gc.auto 0` on all 322 existing session repos (non-destructive, stops the implicit auto-gc re-trigger, does not touch any history).
3. Set autonomous.max_parallel_tasks to 1 (separate operator constraint: single-task-at-a-time execution, unrelated to this bug but now a standing global default — do not change it back to 3 as part of this PRD).

ACTUAL FIX NEEDED (this PRD's real scope — a code fix, not another manual stopgap):
1. Stop output.log (and any other large/append-only live artifacts in a session dir) from being committed on every event, OR commit it in a way that doesn't produce unbounded blob growth (e.g. exclude it from tracker's git tracking entirely and keep it as an untracked file on disk; or truncate/rotate it before each commit; or only commit a bounded tail). Read tracker.go fully first to understand every caller of commit()/the Tracker type and what output.log is actually used for (session resume? diffing? audit?) before deciding — do not break session resume or any feature that reads output.log from the working tree (untracked files still exist on disk and are readable; only git's own history of it needs to stop growing unboundedly).
2. Make gc.auto=0 (or an equivalently safe, bounded setting) the CODE-level default at repo init time for every NEWLY created session repo going forward (tracker.go's init path, ~line 32-42), not just a one-time manual fix on existing repos — the manual `git config gc.auto 0` sweep applied today is a stopgap on EXISTING repos only and does not survive a `datawatch init`-created new session repo tomorrow.
3. Decide and implement what (if anything) should perform actual git maintenance on these session repos now that implicit auto-gc is disabled — e.g. a deliberate, memory-bounded, periodic maintenance path (capped via `pack.windowMemory`, `pack.threads`, or run via a resource-limited subprocess/cgroup so a worst case can never again take down the whole daemon), OR a documented decision that these repos simply never need gc because of the output.log fix in (1) (if excluding output.log from tracking keeps repos small enough that gc is moot). Prefer the simplest fix that actually prevents recurrence — do not over-engineer a maintenance scheduler if excluding output.log alone solves it.
4. Remediate the three already-bloated repos (ab22 30GB, 9245 8.7GB, ddeb 815MB) safely — i.e. NOT by re-running a full in-process repack inside the daemon's own cgroup (that's exactly what already caused the OOM twice). Do this as a separate, explicit, memory-bounded operation run outside the daemon process (e.g. a standalone script invoked directly, with nice/ionice and a pack.windowMemory cap, or simply by removing output.log from each repo's tracked history since it's disposable/live-tail data, which should shrink these repos dramatically without ever needing an expensive delta search across huge blobs). Verify the fix actually shrinks these repos and does not itself OOM anything, before calling this done.
5. Add a regression test asserting that tracker.go's repo-init path sets the safe gc config, and (if feasible) a test proving a simulated large/growing output.log does not get committed as part of git history going forward.
6. Full documentation + CHANGELOG + version bump per this project's existing conventions. File this as BL420 in docs/plans/README.md item 19 — NOTE: item 19 has ALREADY been filed by the operator's session directly (do not duplicate it; read it first and just update/close it with the actual fix detail once shipped).

VERIFICATION REQUIREMENT (non-negotiable — this project's standing rule: never claim a fix works from reading code alone):
- Actually reproduce something close to the failure mode in a disposable test session dir (not against the live ab22/9245/ddeb repos) — grow a fake output.log across many commits, confirm today's code (pre-fix) still trips the same gc/memory pattern at some bounded smaller scale, then confirm the fix prevents it.
- Actually verify the three real bloated repos shrink after remediation (du -sh before/after) and that remediation itself does not spike memory beyond a safe bound (watch `ps`/`systemctl status` RSS during the operation).
- Actually restart the live datawatch daemon after the fix is deployed and confirm no OOM recurs, watching `journalctl --user -u datawatch` and `systemctl --user status datawatch` memory stats for a reasonable observation window.

OUT OF SCOPE for this PRD:
- Any other performance/stability issue not related to this specific git-growth OOM mechanism.
- Re-architecting the Tracker/session model beyond what's needed to stop unbounded git growth.
- Changing autonomous.max_parallel_tasks (already set to 1 by the operator directly; leave it).

This is the first PRD run under the new "all datawatch development work goes through the autonomous PRD system" operating model (operator directive, 2026-10-13) — the operator wants this run closely observed since it's the first one. Use claude-code for decompose, task execution, and verification throughout.
